title: [Chapitre] III. Réseaux via découpages : notes manuscrites (08/06/1986).

errors: The case analysis as transcribed ('T_1 non majoré, T_2 non majoré'; 'T_2' elsewhere) must read T_1 non minoré / minoré and T_n non majoré / majoré. Only the extreme slices T_1 and T_n matter, and the boundedness condition relevant for T_1 is from below.
Edge case n = 0 (X empty) is not covered by n' = (n−1) + ε: there X' = L and n' = 1. The formula tacitly assumes n ≥ 1.

The count tacitly assumes every interstitial slice between T_i ≪ T_{i+1} is nonempty, i.e. that strict separation (≪) guarantees a gap. This is consistent with the notation but not stated on this page.

ideas.what: Counting components of the tame complement of a finite union of separated slices: n' = n−1 + (left end bounded) + (right end bounded), hence |#π0(X) − #π0(X')| ≤ 1
ideas.modern_name: complementary intervals of a finite union of intervals in an o-minimal / ordered line
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (elementary order topology; o-minimality, van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, 1980s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 only sketches 'topologie modérée' in general, without this count

ideas.what: The poset of tame parts with a 'relative tame position' compatibility relation, the subset of 'frank' parts, and the question whether compatibility is determined by the order (via existence of X∧Y)
ideas.modern_name: partial Boolean algebra / orthoposet with compatibility relation; closure operator onto a sub-poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kochen–Specker (partial Boolean algebras, 1960s); orthomodular poset theory (Foulis, Randall, Kalmbach)

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks whether the compatibility relation 'X, Y in relative tame position' on Mod(L) is recoverable from the inclusion order alone, e.g. iff X∧Y exists. He leaves this unanswered. It is an axiomatisation question for the poset of tame subsets: is the order alone enough to reconstruct the tame structure? It parallels known questions in orthomodular posets on whether compatibility is determined by existence of meets.
missed.quote: Cette relation est-elle déterminée par la relation d'ordre — p.ex. {X, Y} mod. ssi X ∩ Y existe ???
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Abstract reconstruction of tame (o-minimal-like) geometries from posets of definable sets, i.e. lattice-theoretic or locale-like presentations of tame topology, is little developed. This is a concrete test question, though in this 1-dimensional ordered setting it is likely elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The completed result is an elementary interval count. The new element is the abstraction of tame parts into an orthocomplemented partial-lattice structure and the open question of whether compatibility is order-determined. That is a mildly interesting unpublished piece of Grothendieck's tame-topology programme, but not a significant missed result.
